ESV.1: “But now, hear my speech, O Job, and listen to all my words.
ESV.2: Behold, I open my mouth; the tongue in my mouth speaks.
ESV.3: My words declare the uprightness of my heart, and what my lips know they speak sincerely.
ESV.4: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
ESV.5: Answer me, if you can; set your words in order before me; take your stand.
ESV.6: Behold, I am toward God as you are; I too was pinched off from a piece of clay.
ESV.7: Behold, no fear of me need terrify you; my pressure will not be heavy upon you.
ESV.8: “Surely you have spoken in my ears, and I have heard the sound of your words.
ESV.9: You say, ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no iniquity in me.
ESV.10: Behold, he finds occasions against me, he counts me as his enemy,
ESV.11: he puts my feet in the stocks and watches all my paths.’
ESV.12: “Behold, in this you are not right. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
ESV.13: Why do you contend against him, saying, ‘He will answer none of man's  words’?
ESV.14: For God speaks in one way, and in two, though man does not perceive it.
ESV.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, while they slumber on their beds,
ESV.16: then he opens the ears of men and terrifies  them with warnings,
ESV.17: that he may turn man aside from his deed and conceal pride from a man;
ESV.18: he keeps back his soul from the pit, his life from perishing by the sword.
ESV.19: “Man is also rebuked with pain on his bed and with continual strife in his bones,
ESV.20: so that his life loathes bread, and his appetite the choicest food.
ESV.21: His flesh is so wasted away that it cannot be seen, and his bones that were not seen stick out.
ESV.22: His soul draws near the pit, and his life to those who bring death.
ESV.23: If there be for him an angel, a mediator, one of the thousand, to declare to man what is right for him,
ESV.24: and he is merciful to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down into the pit; I have found a ransom;
ESV.25: let his flesh become fresh with youth; let him return to the days of his youthful vigor’;
ESV.26: then man  prays to God, and he accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to man his righteousness.
ESV.27: He sings before men and says: ‘I sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not repaid to me.
ESV.28: He has redeemed my soul from going down into the pit, and my life shall look upon the light.’
ESV.29: “Behold, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man,
ESV.30: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be lighted with the light of life.
ESV.31: Pay attention, O Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
ESV.32: If you have any words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.
ESV.33: If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

NKJV.1: “But please, Job, hear my speech, And listen to all my words.
NKJV.2: Now, I open my mouth; My tongue speaks in my mouth.
NKJV.3: My words come from my upright heart; My lips utter pure knowledge.
NKJV.4: The Spirit of God has made me, And the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
NKJV.5: If you can answer me, Set your words in order before me; Take your stand.
NKJV.6: Truly I am as your spokesman before God; I also have been formed out of clay.
NKJV.7: Surely no fear of me will terrify you, Nor will my hand be heavy on you.
NKJV.8: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, And I have heard the sound of your words, saying,
NKJV.9: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am innocent, and there is no iniquity in me.
NKJV.10: Yet He finds occasions against me,  He counts me as His enemy;
NKJV.11: He puts my feet in the stocks, He watches all my paths.’
NKJV.12: “Look, in this you are not righteous. I will answer you, For God is greater than man.
NKJV.13: Why do you contend with Him? For He does not give an accounting of any of His words.
NKJV.14: For God may speak in one way, or in another, Yet man does not perceive it.
NKJV.15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, When deep sleep falls upon men, While slumbering on their beds,
NKJV.16: Then He opens the ears of men, And seals their instruction.
NKJV.17: In order to turn man from his deed, And conceal pride from man,
NKJV.18: He keeps back his soul from the Pit, And his life from perishing by the sword.
NKJV.19: “Man is also chastened with pain on his bed, And with strong pain in many of his bones,
NKJV.20: So that his life abhors bread, And his soul succulent food.
NKJV.21: His flesh wastes away from sight, And his bones stick out which once were not seen.
NKJV.22: Yes, his soul draws near the Pit, And his life to the executioners.
NKJV.23: “If there is a messenger for him, A mediator, one among a thousand, To show man His uprightness,
NKJV.24: Then He is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom’;
NKJV.25: His flesh shall be young like a child’s, He shall return to the days of his youth.
NKJV.26: He shall pray to God, and He will delight in him, He shall see His face with joy, For He restores to man His righteousness.
NKJV.27: Then he looks at men and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted what was right, And it did not profit me.’
NKJV.28: He will redeem his soul from going down to the Pit, And his life shall see the light.
NKJV.29: “Behold, God works all these things, Twice, in fact, three times with a man,
NKJV.30: To bring back his soul from the Pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of life.
NKJV.31: “Give ear, Job, listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will speak.
NKJV.32: If you have anything to say, answer me; Speak, for I desire to justify you.
NKJV.33: If not, listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”

WEB.33: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”

NLT.1:
“Listen to my words, Job;
pay attention to what I have to say.
NLT.2:
Now that I have begun to speak,
let me continue.
NLT.3:
I speak with all sincerity;
I speak the truth.
NLT.4:
For the Spirit of God has made me,
and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
NLT.5:
Answer me, if you can;
make your case and take your stand.
NLT.6:
Look, you and I both belong to God.
I, too, was formed from clay.
NLT.7:
So you don’t need to be afraid of me.
I won’t come down hard on you.
NLT.8:
“You have spoken in my hearing,
and I have heard your very words.
NLT.9:
You said, ‘I am pure; I am without sin;
I am innocent; I have no guilt.
NLT.10:
God is picking a quarrel with me,
and he considers me his enemy.
NLT.11:
He puts my feet in the stocks
and watches my every move.’
NLT.12:
“But you are wrong, and I will show you why.
For God is greater than any human being.
NLT.13:
So why are you bringing a charge against him?
Why say he does not respond to people’s complaints?
NLT.14:
For God speaks again and again,
though people do not recognize it.
NLT.15:
He speaks in dreams, in visions of the night,
when deep sleep falls on people
as they lie in their beds.
NLT.16:
He whispers in their ears
and terrifies them with warnings.
NLT.17:
He makes them turn from doing wrong;
he keeps them from pride.
NLT.18:
He protects them from the grave,
from crossing over the river of death.
NLT.19:
“Or God disciplines people with pain on their sickbeds,
with ceaseless aching in their bones.
NLT.20:
They lose their appetite
for even the most delicious food.
NLT.21:
Their flesh wastes away,
and their bones stick out.
NLT.22:
They are at death’s door;
the angels of death wait for them.
NLT.23:
“But if an angel from heaven appears —
a special messenger to intercede for a person
and declare that he is upright —
NLT.24:
he will be gracious and say,
‘Rescue him from the grave,
for I have found a ransom for his life.’
NLT.25:
Then his body will become as healthy as a child’s,
firm and youthful again.
NLT.26:
When he prays to God,
he will be accepted.
And God will receive him with joy
and restore him to good standing.
NLT.27:
He will declare to his friends,
‘I sinned and twisted the truth,
but it was not worth it.
NLT.28:
God rescued me from the grave,
and now my life is filled with light.’
NLT.29:
“Yes, God does these things
again and again for people.
NLT.30:
He rescues them from the grave
so they may enjoy the light of life.
NLT.31:
Mark this well, Job. Listen to me,
for I have more to say.
NLT.32:
But if you have anything to say, go ahead.
Speak, for I am anxious to see you justified.
NLT.33:
But if not, then listen to me.
Keep silent and I will teach you wisdom!”

AMP.1:
"However, Job, please listen to my words,
And pay attention to everything I say.
AMP.2:
"Behold, I have opened my mouth [to begin my speech];
My tongue in my mouth is going to speak.
AMP.3:
"My words will express the uprightness of my heart,
And my lips will speak what they know with utter sincerity.
AMP.4:
"The Spirit of God has made me,
And the breath of the Almighty gives me life [which inspires me].
AMP.5:
"Answer me, if you can;
Set yourselves before me, take your stand.
AMP.6:
"Behold, I belong to God like you;
I too was formed out of the clay.
AMP.7:
"Behold, I will not make you afraid or terrified of me [for I am only mortal and not God],
Nor should any pressure from me weigh heavily upon you.
AMP.8:
"Surely you have spoken in my hearing,
And I have heard the sound of your words, saying:
AMP.9:
'I am pure, without transgression;
I am innocent and there is no guilt in me.
AMP.10:
'Behold, God finds pretexts against me;
He counts me as His enemy.
AMP.11:
'He puts my feet in the stocks [to hinder and humiliate me];
He [suspiciously] watches all my paths,' [you say].
AMP.12:
"Look, let me answer you, in this you are not right or just;
For God is greater and far superior to man.
AMP.13:
"Why do you complain against Him?
That He does not answer [you with] all His doings.
AMP.14:
"For God speaks once,
And even twice, yet no one notices it [including you, Job].
AMP.15:
"In a dream, a vision of the night [one may hear God's voice],
When deep sleep falls on men
While slumbering upon the bed,
AMP.16:
Then He opens the ears of men
And seals their instruction,
AMP.17:
That He may turn man aside from his conduct,
And keep him from pride;
AMP.18:
He holds back his soul from the pit [of destruction],
And his life from passing over into Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead).
AMP.19:
"Man is also disciplined with pain on his bed,
And with unceasing complaint in his bones,
AMP.20:
So that his life makes him loathe food,
And his soul [loathe] even his favorite dishes.
AMP.21:
"His flesh is so wasted away that it cannot be seen,
And his bones which were not seen now stick out.
AMP.22:
"Then his soul draws near to the pit [of destruction],
And his life to those who bring death (the destroyers).
AMP.23:
"If there is an angel as a mediator for him,
One out of a thousand,
To explain to a man what is right for him [that is, how to be in right standing with God],
AMP.24:
Then the angel is gracious to him, and says,
'Spare him from going down to the pit [of destruction];
I have found a ransom [a consideration, or reason for redemption, an atonement]!'
AMP.25:
"Let his flesh be restored and become fresher than in youth;
Let him return to the days of his youthful strength.
AMP.26:
"He will pray to God, and He shall be favorable to him,
So that he looks at His face with joy;
For God restores to man His righteousness [that is, his right standing with God—with its joys].
AMP.27:
"He sings out to other men,
'I have sinned and perverted that which was right,
And it was not proper for me!
AMP.28:
'God has redeemed my life from going to the pit [of destruction],
And my life shall see the light.'"
AMP.29: [Elihu comments,] "Behold, God does all these things twice, yes, three times, with a man,
AMP.30:
To bring his life back from the pit [of destruction],
That he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
AMP.31:
"Pay attention, Job, listen to me;
Keep silent, and I will speak.
AMP.32:
"If you have anything to say, answer me;
Speak, for I desire to justify you.
AMP.33:
"If not [and you have nothing to say], listen to me;
Keep silent, and I will teach you wisdom."

NRSVCE.1:
“But now, hear my speech, O Job,
and listen to all my words.
NRSVCE.2:
See, I open my mouth;
the tongue in my mouth speaks.
NRSVCE.3:
My words declare the uprightness of my heart,
and what my lips know they speak sincerely.
NRSVCE.4:
The spirit of God has made me,
and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
NRSVCE.5:
Answer me, if you can;
set your words in order before me; take your stand.
NRSVCE.6:
See, before God I am as you are;
I too was formed from a piece of clay.
NRSVCE.7:
No fear of me need terrify you;
my pressure will not be heavy on you.
NRSVCE.8:
“Surely, you have spoken in my hearing,
and I have heard the sound of your words.
NRSVCE.9:
You say, ‘I am clean, without transgression;
I am pure, and there is no iniquity in me.
NRSVCE.10:
Look, he finds occasions against me,
he counts me as his enemy;
NRSVCE.11:
he puts my feet in the stocks,
and watches all my paths.’
NRSVCE.12:
“But in this you are not right. I will answer you:
God is greater than any mortal.
NRSVCE.13:
Why do you contend against him,
saying, ‘He will answer none of my words’?
NRSVCE.14:
For God speaks in one way,
and in two, though people do not perceive it.
NRSVCE.15:
In a dream, in a vision of the night,
when deep sleep falls on mortals,
while they slumber on their beds,
NRSVCE.16:
then he opens their ears,
and terrifies them with warnings,
NRSVCE.17:
that he may turn them aside from their deeds,
and keep them from pride,
NRSVCE.18:
to spare their souls from the Pit,
their lives from traversing the River.
NRSVCE.19:
They are also chastened with pain upon their beds,
and with continual strife in their bones,
NRSVCE.20:
so that their lives loathe bread,
and their appetites dainty food.
NRSVCE.21:
Their flesh is so wasted away that it cannot be seen;
and their bones, once invisible, now stick out.
NRSVCE.22:
Their souls draw near the Pit,

NRSVCE.26:

he comes into his presence with joy,
and God repays him for his righteousness.
NRSVCE.27:
That person sings to others and says,

and it was not paid back to me.
NRSVCE.28:
He has redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit,
and my life shall see the light.’

twice, three times, with mortals,
NRSVCE.30:
to bring back their souls from the Pit,
so that they may see the light of life.

Pay heed, Job, listen to me;
be silent, and I will speak.
NRSVCE.32:
If you have anything to say, answer me;
speak, for I desire to justify you.
NRSVCE.33:
If not, listen to me;
be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

MSG.1:
"So please, Job, hear me out,
honor me by listening to me.
MSG.2:
What I'm about to say
has been carefully thought out.
MSG.3:
I have no ulterior motives in this;
I'm speaking honestly from my heart.
MSG.4:
The Spirit of God made me what I am,
the breath of God Almighty gave me life!
MSG.5:
"And if you think you can prove me wrong, do it.
Lay out your arguments. Stand up for yourself!
MSG.6:
Look, I'm human—no better than you;
we're both made of the same kind of mud.
MSG.7:
So let's work this through together;
don't let my aggressiveness overwhelm you.
MSG.8:
"Here's what you said.
I heard you say it with my own ears.
MSG.9:
You said, 'I'm pure—I've done nothing wrong.
Believe me, I'm clean—my conscience is clear.
MSG.10:
But God keeps picking on me;
he treats me like I'm his enemy.
MSG.11:
He's thrown me in jail;
he keeps me under constant surveillance.'
MSG.12:
"But let me tell you, Job, you're wrong, dead wrong!
God is far greater than any human.
MSG.13:
So how dare you haul him into court,
and then complain that he won't answer your charges?
MSG.14:
God always answers, one way or another,
even when people don't recognize his presence.
MSG.15:
"In a dream, for instance, a vision at night,
when men and women are deep in sleep,
fast asleep in their beds—
MSG.16:
God opens their ears
and impresses them with warnings
MSG.17:
To turn them back from something bad they're planning,
from some reckless choice,
MSG.18:
And keep them from an early grave,
from the river of no return.
MSG.19:
"Or, God might get their attention through pain,
by throwing them on a bed of suffering,
MSG.20:
So they can't stand the sight of food,
have no appetite for their favorite treats.
MSG.21:
They lose weight, wasting away to nothing,
reduced to a bag of bones.
MSG.22:
They hang on the cliff-edge of death,
knowing the next breath may be their last.
MSG.23:
"But even then an angel could come,
a champion—there are thousands of them!—
to take up your cause,
MSG.24:
A messenger who would mercifully intervene,
canceling the death sentence with the words:
'I've come up with the ransom!'
MSG.25:
Before you know it, you're healed,
the very picture of health!
MSG.26:
"Or, you may fall on your knees and pray—to God's delight!
You'll see God's smile and celebrate,
finding yourself set right with God.
MSG.27:
You'll sing God's praises to everyone you meet,
testifying, 'I messed up my life—
and let me tell you, it wasn't worth it.
MSG.28:
But God stepped in and saved me from certain death.
I'm alive again! Once more I see the light!'
MSG.29:
"This is the way God works.
Over and over again
MSG.30:
He pulls our souls back from certain destruction
so we'll see the light—and live in the light!
MSG.31:
"Keep listening, Job.
Don't interrupt—I'm not finished yet.
MSG.32:
But if you think of anything I should know, tell me.
There's nothing I'd like better than to see your name cleared.
MSG.33:
Meanwhile, keep listening. Don't distract me with interruptions.
I'm going to teach you the basics of wisdom."

NET.1: “But now, O Job, listen to my words, and hear everything I have to say!
NET.2: See now, I have opened my mouth; my tongue in my mouth has spoken.
NET.3: My words come from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips will utter knowledge sincerely.
NET.4: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
NET.5: Reply to me, if you can; set your arguments in order before me and take your stand!
NET.6: Look, I am just like you in relation to God; I too have been molded from clay.
NET.7: Therefore no fear of me should terrify you, nor should my pressure be heavy on you.
NET.8: “Indeed, you have said in my hearing (I heard the sound of the words!):
NET.9: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean and have no iniquity.
NET.10: Yet God finds occasions with me; he regards me as his enemy!
NET.11: He puts my feet in shackles; he watches closely all my paths.’
NET.12: Now in this, you are not right — I answer you, for God is greater than a human being.
NET.13: Why do you contend against him, that he does not answer all a person’s words?
NET.14: “For God speaks, the first time in one way, the second time in another, though a person does not perceive it.
NET.15: In a dream, a night vision, when deep sleep falls on people as they sleep in their beds.
NET.16: Then he gives a revelation to people, and terrifies them with warnings,
NET.17: to turn a person from his sin, and to cover a person’s pride.
NET.18: He spares a person’s life from corruption, his very life from crossing over the river.
NET.19: Or a person is chastened by pain on his bed, and with the continual strife of his bones,
NET.20: so that his life loathes food, and his soul rejects appetizing fare.
NET.21: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones, which were not seen, are easily visible.
NET.22: He draws near to the place of corruption, and his life to the messengers of death.
NET.23: If there is an angel beside him, one mediator out of a thousand, to tell a person what constitutes his uprightness;
NET.24: and if God is gracious to him and says, ‘Spare him from going down to the place of corruption, I have found a ransom for him,’
NET.25: then his flesh is restored like a youth’s; he returns to the days of his youthful vigor.
NET.26: He entreats God, and God delights in him, he sees God’s face with rejoicing, and God restores to him his righteousness.
NET.27: That person sings to others, saying: ‘I have sinned and falsified what is right, but I was not punished according to what I deserved.
NET.28: He redeemed my life from going down to the place of corruption, and my life sees the light!’
NET.29: “Indeed, God does all these things, twice, three times, in his dealings with a person,
NET.30: to turn back his life from the place of corruption, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
NET.31: Pay attention, Job — listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
NET.32: If you have any words, reply to me; speak, for I want to justify you.
NET.33: If not, you listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”
